contract.settlement_definition: Seven series, one winner each. Player series (KXNBA3PTCONTEST, KXNBASLAMDUNK, KXNBAALLSTARMVP) settle Yes if the named player wins the stated year's event; a player who drops out, withdraws or does not participate resolves No (not void). Team series settle Yes if the named team wins: KXNBAALLSTARGAME = champion of the 2026 three-team mini-tournament of four 12-minute games: three round-robin games (Game 2/3 pairings depend on Game 1) and Game 4, a championship between the top two; point differential is the first tiebreaker only when all three teams finish 1-1; KXNBARISINGSTARS = winner of a four-team bracket with semifinals to 40 points and a final to 25; KXNBAALLSTAR (2025) and KXNBASHOOTINGSTARS have only a one-line primary rule, so their format, ties and non-participation handling are unstated. The 3PT contest has two rounds of 70-second shooting with three finalists; the dunk contest has four players, two judged dunks per round, two finalists, and only the finalists' two final-round dunks (combined) decide. No rule names a source of truth or treats shoot-offs, dunk-offs, tied championship games or MVP co-winners.

rules_evidence.quote: The top three scorers from the first round advance to the championship round, where the highest score determines the winner.
rules_evidence.establishes: Two-round format with three finalists; final-round score alone decides (round-1 score does not carry over).

rules_evidence.quote: players attempt to score as many points as possible from multiple 3-point locations within 70 seconds
rules_evidence.establishes: The round is timed (70 s) over several locations, so release tempo and location-specific accuracy matter; ball values are not stated.

rules_evidence.quote: If the player drops out, withdraws, or does not participate in the contest for any reason, the market resolves to No.
rules_evidence.establishes: Withdrawal of the named entrant resolves No rather than void, so field-withdrawal hazard maps directly to the No side.

rules_evidence.quote: In the first round, all four players will attempt two dunks, and the combined score will determine the top two who advance to the final round.
rules_evidence.establishes: Four entrants, two judged dunks in round 1, two finalists; judging scale and dunk-off procedure are not stated.

rules_evidence.quote: Each finalist will then attempt two additional dunks, with the higher combined score determining the champion.
rules_evidence.establishes: Final is decided on the two final-round dunks' combined score only; tie handling is unstated.

rules_evidence.quote: The Pro Basketball All-Star Game will feature a round-robin mini-tournament with four 12-minute games.
rules_evidence.establishes: 2026 game market is a tournament champion market over timed 12-minute games, not a single game and not a target-score format.

rules_evidence.quote: If all three teams finish 1-1 after the round-robin games, the first tiebreaker will be point differential across each team’s two games.
rules_evidence.establishes: Margins, not only wins, matter for advancement; later tiebreakers (if point differential ties) are not stated.

rules_evidence.quote: Game 4: All-Star Championship (top two teams from round-robin play)
rules_evidence.establishes: A championship game between the top two round-robin teams decides the series; round-robin record alone does not settle it.

rules_evidence.quote: Semifinal games are won by the first team to reach or exceed 40 points, and the Championship is won by the first team to reach or exceed 25 points.
rules_evidence.establishes: Rising Stars uses untimed target-score races (40 then 25), so a race-to-target model, not a margin-per-minute model, applies.
The rule anticipates rescheduling: settlement follows the event even if moved; a cancellation path is not stated.

rules_evidence.quote: If Brandon Ingram wins the 2026 Pro Basketball All-Star MVP, then the market resolves to Yes.
rules_evidence.establishes: MVP market settles on the official All-Star MVP award for the event; selection method and co-winner handling are unstated.

rules_evidence.quote: If Team Knicks wins the 2026 Pro Basketball All-Star Shooting Stars contest
rules_evidence.establishes: Shooting Stars entrants are franchise-named teams; no format, scoring or withdrawal clause is given in the rules text.

rules_evidence.quote: If Shaq's OGs wins the NBA All-Star Game, then the market resolves to Yes.
rules_evidence.establishes: 2025 game market names a drafted team (four-team format that year); rules give no format, so the target-score structure is from memory.

variants_and_edge_cases: Withdrawal: 3PT, dunk and MVP rules say a non-participating named player resolves No; the four team series contain no such clause, so a renamed or merged team is unhandled.
KXNBAALLSTARGAME 2026: point differential is the first tiebreaker only for a 1-1/1-1/1-1 round robin; the next tiebreaker and overtime in a tied 12-minute game are not in the text.

KXNBAALLSTAR 2025 versus KXNBAALLSTARGAME 2026: same contract type, different formats (2025 four drafted teams with target-score games from memory; 2026 timed round robin quoted), so history cannot be pooled without the format vector.
KXNBARISINGSTARS: semifinals end at 40, final at 25 (race formats, no clock); the event was 'originally scheduled' for a date, so postponement keeps the market alive; cancellation is unstated.
3PT contest: the final-round score decides; round-1 ties for third place and final-round ties (shoot-off) are not described in the rules.
Dunk contest: judging scale, number of judges, attempt limits and dunk-off on ties are not in the rules; only round structure is.

KXNBASHOOTINGSTARS: Kalshi's rules_secondary is empty and its text gives only the team name and event date. The league's official 2026 rules PDF supplies team size, scoring, rounds, tiebreakers and violations, but Kalshi does not say it adopts them, so ties, disqualification (which a team can incur for a missing valid attempt or out-of-order shooting), replay and cancellation handling stay unknown for settlement.
MVP: no statement of whether the award covers the championship game or the whole tournament, how it is chosen, or co-MVP treatment.
Celebrity Game is no longer claimed: no live Kalshi series exists for it in the evidence pack.
contract.settlement_data_source: Not named in any sampled rule; assumed to be the NBA's official announcement of each event's winner and of the All-Star MVP (NBA.com results/press release). Kalshi's own determination governs if it differs.

mechanism.summary: Seven series settle on the winner of a one-off All-Star Weekend event: two individual skills contests (3PT, dunk), a team shooting contest (Shooting Stars), three team exhibition tournaments (2026 All-Star round robin, 2025 four-team All-Star, Rising Stars bracket) and an award (All-Star MVP). The outcome is generated in layers: the league, voters and honorary coaches form fields and rosters; withdrawal resolves a named player's market to No; entrants produce performance (timed rack shooting, judged dunks, low-defence scoring in timed 12-minute games or untimed races to 40/25); the format converts performances to a champion through rounds, tiebreaks such as point differential, and finals; the MVP is then chosen by a panel, by convention (not by rule) almost always from the champion's players. Winners are maxima over noisy scores or short high-variance games, so favourites are capped and format parameters matter as much as skill. Regular-season counting-stat machinery is mostly irrelevant; each series uses its own scoped inputs (contract.series_input_scope).

stages.name: Field and roster formation
stages.description: Fields and rosters are produced by invitation (contests), fan/player/media votes and coach reserve picks (All-Star Game), nationality-based team assignment (2026 USA Stars, USA Stripes, World), honorary-coach drafts (Rising Stars, 2025 ASG teams), franchise teams (Shooting Stars) and commissioner injury replacements. Withdrawals and doubling up change the set until the day before. For 3PT, dunk and MVP a withdrawn named player resolves No, so participation probability multiplies every Yes price.
stages.distribution: Discrete set membership; withdrawal is a Bernoulli per entrant with correlated risk when an entrant also plays the Game.

stages.name: Contest skill: location-specific rack shooting, tempo and dunk repertoire
stages.description: In the 3PT contest each shooter has 70 seconds (rules) for racks at several locations with no defender; skill is per-location make probability, deep-range accuracy for bonus balls, choice of the all-money-ball rack location and release tempo, since unreleased balls score zero. In the dunk contest the analogue is the repertoire of difficulty tiers and conversion within attempts. Season box scores predict these only through open catch-and-shoot and location splits plus prior contest record.
stages.distribution: Per-ball Bernoulli with positive within-round correlation (beta-binomial); dunk make is Bernoulli by tier with a miss penalty, so scores are a bimodal mixture.

stages.name: Contest format aggregation: rounds, advancement, final reset and shoot-offs
stages.description: Round scores become a winner through the format: in the 3PT contest the top three of round one advance and the final-round score alone decides (rules), so round-one scores do not carry; in the dunk contest the top two of four advance and the two final dunks decide. Ties go to shoot-offs or dunk-offs that the rules do not describe. The maximum over noisy scores means the best shooter wins well under half the time.
stages.distribution: Discrete scores with ties; the winner is an extreme-value statistic over finalists, so upset probability is high and shoot-offs are not rare.

stages.name: Judging of dunks
stages.description: Judges score each dunk on a bounded scale, so a dunk's value is a function of difficulty, execution, creativity and crowd response, and scores compress near the top. The panel's composition (former players, celebrities), the sequence of contestants and the use of props all shift scores, and per the rules round-one combined scores only select the two finalists, after which the two final-round dunks alone decide the champion; dunk-offs on ties are not in the rules.
stages.distribution: Ordinal bounded scores with heavy ceiling mass; ties common; panel effects shared across all contestants.

stages.name: Exhibition team strength: All-Star and Rising Stars rosters, minutes and effort
stages.description: Each exhibition team's scoring edge comes from the offence, shooting and creation of players who actually play capped minutes under low defensive effort. All-Star teams are star rosters split by nationality (2026) or by draft (2025); Rising Stars teams are first/second-year players plus a G League team with noisy, cross-league ratings. Effort and variance depend on the regime: timed 12-minute games versus untimed races to a target, which must be estimated separately.
stages.distribution: Timed games: roughly normal margin with large SD per 12 minutes and late compression; target games: first-passage race with discrete 2/3-point jumps.

stages.name: Tournament path: 2026 round robin and target-score brackets
stages.description: Champion probability for KXNBAALLSTARGAME follows the quoted path: Game 1 USA Stars vs World, Game 2 USA Stripes vs the winner, Game 3 USA Stripes vs the loser, then a championship between the top two; a 1-1-1 tie goes to point differential, so blowout margins matter. KXNBARISINGSTARS and the 2025 KXNBAALLSTAR chain two races (semifinals to 40, final to 25), and in 2025 the Rising Stars winner entered the ASG bracket.
stages.distribution: Sequential multi-game path; champion distribution is a mixture over round-robin outcomes, with margin-sum tiebreak creating dependence between games.

stages.name: Shooting Stars team contest
stages.description: Franchise-named teams of shooters (recent editions mixed current players with retired or other-league shooters) score made shots from a sequence of locations against a clock; the higher team score wins. Kalshi's rules give only the team name and event date. The 2026 league format is taken from the official NBA rules PDF (read 2026-11-09): four trios of two NBA players and one NBA Legend; seven locations in fixed order worth 2/2/2/3/2/3/4 points; a 1:10 clock; two rounds with the top two of four advancing, the lower round-1 team shooting first in the final; a 30-second first-round tiebreaker among tied teams and a full 1:10 final tiebreaker; out-of-order shots do not count and a team is disqualified for missing a valid attempt at a location or for shooting from locations out of order. Kalshi's text gives only the team name and date, so how Kalshi treats ties, disqualification, replay or cancellation is unknown.
stages.distribution: Sum over team members of correlated timed make processes; discrete scores with a winner over few teams and possible ties; format-dependent.

stages.name: All-Star MVP selection
stages.description: After the tournament a selection panel names the All-Star MVP, historically almost always a player from the winning team with the standout scoring line or a strong narrative such as a home-market star. P(MVP) is therefore the champion probability times the conditional choice among that team's players, driven by usage and minutes in short games; a withdrawn named player resolves No. 2026 check: the media panel votes right after the championship game and the fan vote counts 25% (Edwards won 10 of 14 panel votes); the award covered the whole three-game tournament, not the final alone, so popularity enters through the in-game fan vote (nba.asg_mvp_fan_vote_share), a separate ballot from the January starter vote.
stages.distribution: Categorical over roughly 8-12 players per champion team, highly concentrated on one or two players once the champion is known; heavy uncertainty pregame.

stages.name: Settlement
stages.description: Each series settles on the officially announced winner. Rules text confirms withdrawal-to-No for the player series, the 2026 round-robin structure with a 1-1-1 point-differential tiebreak and championship game, and the Rising Stars 40/25 targets, but is silent on the next tiebreaker, overtime in tied 12-minute games, shoot-offs, dunk-offs, MVP co-winners and the Kalshi-specific handling of Shooting Stars ties, disqualification and cancellation or any format for the 2025 game; the 2026 Shooting Stars format itself comes from the league's rules PDF, not Kalshi's text.
stages.distribution: Deterministic given the official result; ambiguity mass sits in rare branches (later tiebreakers, ties, cancellation, renamed teams).

talent_strength.note: Per series: dunk pedigree, All-Star and Rising Stars team strength, Shooting Stars team skill.

opponent_matchup.note: Only the team exhibitions have a real opponent (pairwise margins and round-robin pairings); the skills contests have no head-to-head defence.

role_personnel.note: Field and roster membership, minutes plans, MVP shot share.

availability_news.note: Injuries and announcements before the weekend.

coaching_scheme.note: Coaches of exhibitions only set rotations/minutes sharing; no scheme. Contests have no coaches.

environment.note: Neutral site; venue-year sightline/rim offset for the shooting contests only.

game_context_script.note: Round-robin margin incentives, race-to-target ends and timed late effort.

pace_volume.note: Exhibition pace by regime; balls released within 70 s in the 3PT contest.

efficiency_conversion.note: Make rates by location and dunk conversion under contest conditions.

distribution_variance.note: Round-score distributions, judge compression, tournament path mixtures.

situational_schedule_motivation.note: Effort and motivation (prize money, doubling up across Rising Stars, contests and the Game, home-market entrants) have no measurable pregame proxy defined for any of the seven series.

officiating_rules.note: Dunk judges and MVP panel are the adjudicators; format rules decide ties.

settlement_contract.note: Rules sampled for all seven series; two have primary text only (gaps in unresolved).

catalog_entry.label: NBA All-Star Weekend events
catalog_entry.target: Winner of an All-Star Weekend contest or exhibition game
catalog_entry.mechanism: Each All-Star Weekend series settles on the winner of a one-off event: rosters and fields come from votes, drafts and invitations, and a withdrawn named player resolves No; performance is timed rack shooting, judged dunks, team shooting relays, or low-defence exhibition games that are either timed 12-minute round-robin games (point-differential tiebreak) or races to 40/25; the format turns performance into a champion and the MVP is chosen by a panel, almost always (by convention, not rule) from the champion's players. Inputs are scoped per series because the processes are disjoint.

inputs.why: Format parameters decide scoring scale, ties and the number of rounds, so they define what a win means in each series.
Simulated winner distribution over rounds, advancement and shoot-offs is the direct model of the 3-point contest.
Contest make rate is a catch-and-shoot skill without a defender; this input converts game stats to that setting.
The dunk series settles on panel scores, so judge behaviour and ties are the mechanism.
Dunk tier choice and make rate under attempt caps drive expected judged score.
Only pregame talent measure for contestants who rarely appear in season statistics.
Team strength of the actual All-Star rosters in an exhibition environment.
Exhibition margin variance and late effort set how much talent gap converts to a win.
Who plays and how many minutes in each game of the format changes the effective roster.
Contest fields change before the event, shifting every entrant's winning probability.
Selection, captains and participation determine who is on each roster and which events they enter.
Reserve selection and injury replacement set roster membership that feeds roster strength.
Player impact ratings feed the roster strength composite for both All-Star Game series (2026 round robin and 2025 four-team event).
Injury reports before the weekend drive withdrawals and replacement players across all three events.
Announcements on field, captains, format and participation arrive as news before official lists.
All-Star Game only: three-point volume shapes roster offence in a high-3PA exhibition; not used for the contest.
Open-shot make probability by shot type is the best game-data proxy for rack shooting.
Hot-hand dispersion of makes inside a minute-long round sets contest score variance.
Free-throw skill is a low-noise proxy for shooting form in a defender-free setting.
Arena sightlines, backdrop and rim feel shift contest conversion for all entrants.
Format changes announced by the league alter scoring rules for the Game and contests.
Announcement timing of rosters, fields and format sets the as-of date for every input.
Rules fix withdrawal-to-No, the 70 s round, dunk rounds, the 12-minute round robin and 40/25 targets; two series have primary text only.
Official winner announcements are the labels and need reconciling with the contract source.
Location splits, deep-ball rate, rack placement and release tempo convert a shooter to the 70-second contest's scoring.
Round-robin and bracket simulation turns pairwise team gaps into champion probabilities, including the point-differential tiebreak.
Rising Stars and the 2025 game are races to 40/25, which a margin-per-minute model cannot represent.
Rising Stars teams of first/second-year and G League players need their own shrunk, cross-league strength rating.
Shooting Stars is a team shooting contest whose format is unverified; this input carries team skill and the format flag.
MVP is champion probability times the panel's choice among winning-team players.
Home-market or farewell narratives shift the MVP panel's choice among champion-team players.
Shot share inside the exhibition decides who posts the standout line that wins MVP.
Carries the 25% in-game fan vote that decides KXNBAALLSTARMVP alongside the media panel.

interactions.hypothesis: Small per-ball edges compound into only a modest winner probability because the max over about eight noisy round scores caps favourites.
Difficulty beats polish only when the panel's top-score compression is low; with lenient panels a clean easy dunk ties a hard one.
A real roster gap converts to wins less in a short high-variance game, so the same gap gives a lower win probability at 12-minute length than at 48.
Entrant injury status shifts both his own winning chance and the rest of the field through the replacement draw.
With nationality-built teams one side can be systematically stronger, and the point-differential tiebreak rewards a team that blows out the weakest team, not just wins.
MVP probability is roughly champion probability times within-team choice, so a star on a weak team is capped by his team's path.

nba.contest_format_rules_ledger.label: All-Star Weekend format and rules ledger by event and year
nba.contest_format_rules_ledger.mechanism: Each event's winner is a deterministic function of the format: racks, balls, money-ball value, time limit, number of rounds, how many advance, tiebreak or shoot-off, dunk attempt caps and judging scale, All-Star Game length, target score and team structure.
nba.contest_format_rules_ledger.rationale: The formats are changed almost every few years (the Game has switched between East-West, captains' draft and a multi-team mini-tournament), so a historical result is only a label for the same process if the format parameters are matched. The subtle part is that a rule change moves variance and ties, not just level: a shorter game or a single-elimination final increases upset probability.
nba.contest_format_rules_ledger.measurement: Per event-year and per series (3PT, dunk, ASG, Rising Stars, Shooting Stars, MVP): participants, rounds, advancement count, balls per rack, racks, points per ball type (regular, money ball, deep-zone ball), seconds per round, shoot-off rule, dunks per round and attempt limit, judge count and score range, ASG game length or target score, number of teams, team-assignment rule (conference, draft, nationality), round-robin tiebreak order, Rising Stars semifinal/final targets, Shooting Stars team size and scoring, MVP selection method. Each field carries a provenance flag: RULES_TEXT (quoted Kalshi rule, e.g. 70 s, 40/25 targets, 1-1-1 point-differential tiebreak), LEAGUE_RELEASE, or SOURCE_UNVERIFIED; as-of = the league announcement date. Every historical label joins to its own format vector.
free_sources: NBA.com and NBA Communications press releases
nba.contest_format_rules_ledger.why: Format parameters set the tie, upset and score-scale behaviour of all three Kalshi series; without them past winners cannot be pooled.

sources.name: NBA 2026 Kia Shooting Stars official rules (PDF): format, 7 locations and 2/3/4 point values, 1:10 clock, tiebreakers, violations
sources.note: primary source for the 2026 event; verbatim extract and rendered-table reading in completeness/source_provenance/; says nothing about how Kalshi settles ties, disqualification, replay or cancellation

nba.threept_contest_score_pmf.label: Three-Point Contest round-score distribution and winner simulation
nba.threept_contest_score_pmf.mechanism: Each shooter's round score is a sum over racks of correlated Bernoulli makes with different point weights; the winner is the maximum over finalists after advancement, with ties broken by a shoot-off.
nba.threept_contest_score_pmf.rationale: The winner is a max-of-noisy-scores over a field of about eight, so the favourite's chance is capped well below his skill edge; the round-score SD is several points, comparable to the skill gap between the best and median shooter (per-ball make probability is a parameter to be estimated, not a fact). Only the final-round score decides (rules), so round-1 advancement variance and final-round tie mass both matter.
nba.threept_contest_score_pmf.measurement: For each entrant simulate ball by ball: P(make) per location from nba.threept_spot_and_tempo_profile (regular, money-ball and deep-zone balls), the shooter's chosen all-money-ball rack location, balls actually released within 70 s from the tempo distribution (unreleased balls score 0), rack-level correlation rho with a beta-binomial prior from nba.within_game_make_dispersion, point weights from nba.contest_format_rules_ledger; run 20000 simulations of round 1, top-three advancement, final round (score resets) and a shoot-off on ties; output P(win), P(advance). As-of = last field change or rack-placement announcement.
free_sources: Own simulation from public shooting data
nba.threept_contest_score_pmf.why: Directly produces the winner distribution the contest series settles on, including tie mass and field-size effects.

nba.contest_shooting_skill_transfer.label: Transfer of shooter skill to the contest's rack conditions
nba.contest_shooting_skill_transfer.mechanism: Contest make probability is stationary-catch-and-shoot skill from fixed rack spots, with no defender, no movement, rhythm over about a minute and fatigue; it is only partly predicted by game 3P%.
nba.contest_shooting_skill_transfer.rationale: Game 3P% mixes shot difficulty and defence, so contest make rate is better proxied by catch-and-shoot or open-shot 3P%, free-throw skill and past contest make rate, each shrunk because contest samples are 25 balls. Deep-range pull-up shooters can underperform because the contest rewards form repeatability, and a venue's backdrop and rims add a shared level shift.
nba.contest_shooting_skill_transfer.measurement: Per entrant: posterior make rate = precision-weighted mean of (a) catch-and-shoot 3P% on open and wide-open attempts, last 3 seasons, half-life 1 season, shrunk toward league mean with a prior strength k (placeholder 300 attempts, to be fitted by cross-validation on past contests), (b) FT% logit scaled by a fitted slope, (c) past contest make rate shrunk with k (placeholder 75 balls); contest-conditions offset = mean residual of all entrants in the same contest-year (venue-year effect); units = P(make) per ball before location adjustment; as-of = day before.
free_sources: NBA Stats shooting splits by closest defender
Past contest box scores on NBA.com
raw_data: Catch-and-shoot attempts and makes by defender distance
nba.contest_shooting_skill_transfer.why: Different from in-game 3P% because the contest strips out the defender and movement, so the right skill measure for the series is not the default player shooting input.

nba.dunk_judge_score_model.label: Dunk Contest judging panel score and tiebreak model
nba.dunk_judge_score_model.mechanism: The winner is selected by a panel's subjective scores per dunk; round-one two-dunk totals pick the two finalists and the finalists' two final-round dunks alone decide the champion (rules); panel composition, scoring scale and the compression of scores near the maximum decide who wins and whether a dunk-off is needed.
nba.dunk_judge_score_model.rationale: Scores cluster at the top of the scale so many dunks tie, and a run of 10s from celebrity judges can erase a difficulty advantage. Judges anchor on crowd reaction and narrative as well as difficulty, creating a first-mover and last-mover effect, and repeat winners can be penalised or rewarded depending on the panel's era.
nba.dunk_judge_score_model.measurement: From past contests extract every dunk's judge scores; fit an ordinal model of dunk score on (attempt number, make flag, prop use, dunker's reputation, round, panel mean leniency) with a partial-pooling judge effect; estimate per-panel mean and SD and the probability of a perfect score; store panel composition as announced (as-of = announcement); output expected round-one totals, P(advance), final-round two-dunk totals (round one does not carry over) and P(tie) per finalist pair. Use only rounds since the current scale was introduced.
free_sources: NBA.com contest recaps with judge scores
nba.dunk_judge_score_model.why: The series settles on judges' scores, so the process is scoring behaviour and not athletic ability alone.

nba.dunk_difficulty_make_model.label: Dunk difficulty tier and make probability under attempt caps
nba.dunk_difficulty_make_model.mechanism: A contestant's score depends on choosing a dunk of a given difficulty tier and converting it within the attempt allowance; misses burn time or attempts and zero or lower the score.
nba.dunk_difficulty_make_model.rationale: Hard dunks have a high ceiling but a real miss rate, and the attempt cap makes the score a mixture between a clean mid-tier dunk and a failed high-tier one. Props, teammate assists and limited rehearsal affect conversion; contestants who tend to over-script get penalised for misses.
nba.dunk_difficulty_make_model.measurement: Classify each past dunk by difficulty tier (360 or windmill, leap over a person, double-ball, two-step, prop-assisted) from video-coded tags; compute per-dunker attempt success by tier with Beta(2,2) shrinkage, and expected score per dunk = P(make before cap) times mean judged score of the tier plus (1 - P) times the miss score; as-of = last contest participated; units = points per dunk.
nba.dunk_difficulty_make_model.why: Converts a dunker's repertoire into expected judged score under the series' own attempt rules.

nba.dunker_pedigree_profile.label: Dunker athletic profile and prior contest record
nba.dunker_pedigree_profile.mechanism: Contest strength comes from leaping ability, creativity and show experience, none of which appear in regular-season box scores.
nba.dunker_pedigree_profile.rationale: Contest entrants are often bench or G League players whose NBA stats say little, so talent is measured by prior contest finishes, highlight dunk rate, vertical measures from draft combine and age. The sample is tiny and selection is heavy, so pedigree must be shrunk toward a field mean and treated as a ranking, not a number.
nba.dunker_pedigree_profile.measurement: Per announced entrant: pedigree = mean of within-field percentile ranks of (a) contest score = sum over prior contests of points (win 3, final 2, appeared 1) * 0.7^(years since), (b) max vertical z-score from the Draft Combine (missing: field mean plus a missing flag with 0 weight), (c) dunks per 100 minutes over the last two seasons (NBA plus G League), shrunk to the position mean with prior weight 200 minutes; equal weights 1/3 each, plus a G League/non-NBA flag reported separately. Rank within the announced field; as-of = field announcement date.
free_sources: NBA Draft Combine measurements (drafted players only)
Basketball-Reference and G League play-by-play dunk counts
raw_data: In-game dunk counts (NBA and G League)
nba.dunker_pedigree_profile.why: Gives the only pregame talent signal for a contest where season performance is nearly irrelevant.

nba.asg_roster_strength_composite.label: All-Star Game team roster strength and composition
nba.asg_roster_strength_composite.mechanism: The Game winner is the team whose assigned players are collectively better at scoring in an open-court, low-defence environment, built from impact, shooting and creation of the players who actually appear.
nba.asg_roster_strength_composite.rationale: Because the same selected stars are split among teams, gaps are small and dominated by composition: shooters and creators gain more than rim protectors in a low-defence game, and replacements change rosters late. In 2026 teams were built by nationality (USA Stars, USA Stripes, World), so one team can be systematically stronger, unlike a draft; in 2025 the drafted teams faced a Rising Stars team of first/second-year players.
nba.asg_roster_strength_composite.measurement: For each team sum over rostered players minutes_share_i * (0.6*OffImpact_i + 0.25*z(3PA per 36 * 3P%) + 0.15*z(AST%)), where OffImpact_i is multi-season offensive RAPM/EPM shrunk to 0 with prior weight 1,500 possessions; minutes_share from nba.asg_minutes_rotation_plan normalised to 1. Convert the team difference to expected margin per 12 minutes with a scale factor fitted by one-parameter ridge regression on past exhibition margins (2013-2025, pooled over formats; the three weights are fixed, not fitted), applying a -0.5 point adjustment per missing big. As-of = final roster after the replacement window; output every team pair.
raw_data: Player offensive impact per 100 possessions (RAPM/EPM or on/off)
nba.asg_roster_strength_composite.why: Defines which side is stronger under this exhibition's roster assignment, not a league-wide team rating.

nba.asg_effort_scoring_baseline.label: All-Star exhibition effort, pace and score variance baseline, conditional on timed vs target format
nba.asg_effort_scoring_baseline.mechanism: Exhibition scoring and margin come from low defensive effort, extreme three-point volume and random clustering of makes; how effort evolves depends on whether the game is clock-timed (2026: 12-minute games) or untimed race-to-target (2025 ASG, Rising Stars).
nba.asg_effort_scoring_baseline.rationale: Margin variance is large relative to talent gaps, so short games raise the weaker roster's chance. In timed games effort rises in the final minutes and point differential can matter for the tiebreak; in target-score games there is no clock and the end is a race, so the two regimes must not be pooled. The contract year fixes the regime: 2026 KXNBAALLSTARGAME is timed (rules text), KXNBARISINGSTARS is target (rules text).
nba.asg_effort_scoring_baseline.measurement: Split all exhibition games by format vector from nba.contest_format_rules_ledger. Timed games: points per team per minute, 3PA rate, margin SD per 12 minutes and late-compression coefficient (margin SD change over the final 4 minutes). Target games: points per possession for each team and possessions to reach the target, fed to nba.target_score_race_model. Shrink current-format estimates toward the pooled same-regime value (few games per format); as-of = last completed event; units = points and margin SD.
raw_data: All-Star and Rising Stars team points by period
Lead/score history by minute or play-by-play
nba.asg_effort_scoring_baseline.why: Sets how much randomness separates the stronger team from the weaker one in this exhibition.

nba.asg_minutes_rotation_plan.label: All-Star Game minutes plan, rest and multi-game fatigue
nba.asg_minutes_rotation_plan.mechanism: All-Star players play capped minutes with fairly even distribution, and in a multi-game format starters and replacements are managed across games, which changes who is on court in the decisive game.
nba.asg_minutes_rotation_plan.rationale: Minutes are not set by merit: coaches are mostly told to share minutes, and players with injuries or heavy loads often log little. In a mini-tournament, a team that must play two games may rotate its stars, while the fresh final-game lineup matters more than the roster list.
nba.asg_minutes_rotation_plan.measurement: For each All-Star in the final roster: rank-based minutes prior m0 = mean All-Star minutes of past players in the same season-minutes tercile and starter/reserve role (2010+), shrunk to the pooled mean with prior weight 10 player-games. Fit a logistic model for P(minutes < 15) on age, season minutes per game (z), starter flag and an injury-flag dummy (Questionable/Probable listed by 24h before tip) with ridge penalty 1.0; for multi-game formats add the fitted game-2 minus game-1 minutes drop by tercile. As-of = last injury-report vintage at least 2 hours before tip; units = minutes and probability of reduced role.
raw_data: All-Star minutes by player and year
nba.asg_minutes_rotation_plan.why: Needed because the exhibition winner depends on who actually plays and for how long, which can differ sharply from the roster.

nba.asw_field_withdrawal_hazard.label: Contest field changes: withdrawal and replacement hazard
nba.asw_field_withdrawal_hazard.mechanism: The entrant list for the 3-point and dunk contests is announced weeks ahead and changes through injury, rest, ASG replacement and sponsor negotiation, which changes both the field strength and the winner's probability.
nba.asw_field_withdrawal_hazard.rationale: A late replacement is usually weaker or different in type, and a withdrawal of the favourite lifts every remaining entrant; the market question requires a specific named player so this is also an eligibility risk.
nba.asw_field_withdrawal_hazard.measurement: Per announced entrant: base withdrawal rate w0 = (withdrawals + 1)/(announced entrants + 8) counted over 3PT/dunk/skills fields 2010-2026 from NBA.com announcements; logistic update with covariates current injury status (Out/Doubtful/Questionable from nba.injuries_pit at the latest vintage), also-in-All-Star-Game flag and also-in-Rising-Stars flag, ridge 1.0. P(participates) = 1 - P(withdraw). P(win | participates) from the contest score model for the actual announced field; replacements drawn from the next-ranked non-entrants by prior contest pedigree. As-of = each daily injury report and announcement time.
free_sources: ESPN and The Athletic reporting archives
raw_data: Announced contest field by date and year
Entrant also in All-Star Game or Rising Stars flag
nba.asw_field_withdrawal_hazard.why: Winner probabilities depend on the final field, so field risk is its own input in these series.

nba.threept_spot_and_tempo_profile.label: Three-point contest location, deep-ball and release-tempo profile per shooter
nba.threept_spot_and_tempo_profile.mechanism: Contest score depends on accuracy at each rack location, on deep-range accuracy for the bonus balls between racks, on where the shooter places the all-money-ball rack, and on how many balls he releases before 70 seconds expire.
nba.threept_spot_and_tempo_profile.rationale: Pooled open 3P% hides location splits: a corner specialist gains by placing the all-money rack in his best corner, and the deep bonus balls reward a 27+ ft make rate that many spot-up shooters lack. The 70-second limit (rules) means slow releasers leave balls unshot, a zero that pooled accuracy never sees.
nba.threept_spot_and_tempo_profile.measurement: Per shooter: map shotchartdetail 3PA coordinates (LOC_X, LOC_Y) to the five contest racks (corner left/right, wing left/right, top) by distance from the rack position; 3P% by rack over the last 3 seasons shrunk to the shooter's pooled 3P% with k estimated by method of moments (default 150 attempts until estimated), 27+ ft 3P% shrunk to the league deep rate with k estimated (default 100). Tempo = balls released per round and seconds remaining from his past contest rounds (median and sd); if none, impute from the median of previous contestants with a similar release speed from tracking (labelled imputed). Rack placement = announced choice, else the rack maximising expected points. Output P(make) by ball type and balls released; as-of: rack announcement.
free_sources: NBA Stats shot dashboard and shot-location splits
raw_data: shot-level 3PA with x,y location and distance
nba.threept_spot_and_tempo_profile.why: Converts a shooter into the contest's own scoring geometry and time limit, which the series settles on.

nba.asg_tournament_path_sim.label: All-Star / Rising Stars tournament path simulation (round robin, tiebreaks, final)
nba.asg_tournament_path_sim.mechanism: Champion probability is the result of a multi-game path: in 2026 three teams play a round robin of 12-minute games where margins feed the point-differential tiebreak, then the top two play a championship; brackets (Rising Stars, 2025 ASG) chain two target-score races.
nba.asg_tournament_path_sim.rationale: A pairwise team gap is not a winner probability: in the 2026 round robin a team's chance depends on its margin distribution in two games (point differential decides a 1-1-1 tie, per rules) and on who it meets in the final; Game 2/3 pairings depend on Game 1's result, so the path is sequential. In 2025 the fourth ASG team was the Rising Stars winner, an entrant unknown until two days before.
nba.asg_tournament_path_sim.measurement: Monte Carlo (50,000 runs) over the format vector from nba.contest_format_rules_ledger: for timed games draw margin ~ Normal(expected margin from nba.asg_roster_strength_composite adjusted for minutes, SD from nba.asg_effort_scoring_baseline); apply the Game-2/Game-3 pairing by Game-1 result; rank by record then point differential and break remaining ties randomly (flagged); play the championship; for target-score formats call nba.target_score_race_model per game. Where the entrant list is not yet announced, draw each entrant from the nba.rising_stars_roster_strength rank order, never from market prices. Output P(champion) and P(final) per team; as-of = last roster change.
free_sources: Format parameters from the rules ledger
Basketball-Reference All-Star box scores for calibration
raw_data: Pairwise expected margins from roster-strength input
nba.asg_tournament_path_sim.why: Directly produces the champion probability that KXNBAALLSTARGAME, KXNBAALLSTAR and KXNBARISINGSTARS settle on.

nba.target_score_race_model.label: Race-to-target exhibition game model (first to 40 / first to 25)
nba.target_score_race_model.mechanism: In an untimed game the winner is the first team to reach or exceed a target score, so the outcome is a first-passage race of two scoring processes rather than a margin over fixed time.
nba.target_score_race_model.rationale: A race to 25 has few possessions, so a per-possession efficiency edge converts to a much smaller win probability than in a 48-minute game, and a single three or and-one near the target is decisive (a made shot can overshoot). There is no garbage time and no clock-driven fouling, so timed-game variance estimates do not transfer. Relation to the existing nba.first_passage_race_table: that input is a first-to-N race inside a regular 48-minute game at full effort and does not end the game; here reaching the target ends the game at exhibition effort, so the table is only a structural prior/cross-check for N=25 and is not reused as the estimate.
nba.target_score_race_model.measurement: Model each possession as points in {0,1,2,3,4} with team-specific probabilities from offensive rating vs opponent defence under exhibition effort (from nba.asg_effort_scoring_baseline target-regime estimates), alternate possessions with a possession-start Bernoulli, simulate to target T (40 semifinal, 25 final per KXNBARISINGSTARS rules) 20000 times; output P(win) and expected possessions; validate on past target-score exhibitions; units = probability.
free_sources: NBA.com play-by-play of Rising Stars and 2024-2025 All-Star target games
nba.target_score_race_model.why: Rising Stars (quoted 40/25 targets) and the 2025 ASG are races, so their winner requires this model.

nba.rising_stars_roster_strength.label: Rising Stars team strength from first/second-year and G League rosters
nba.rising_stars_roster_strength.mechanism: Rising Stars teams are drafted from first- and second-year NBA players plus a G League team, so team strength rests on young-player offensive ratings with small samples and a cross-league adjustment for the G League side.
nba.rising_stars_roster_strength.rationale: Rookie and sophomore impact estimates are noisy and the G League team's stats are in a weaker league, so naive per-game scoring over-rates high-usage players on bad teams and mis-rates the G League side. Honorary coaches draft the teams, so team balance depends on the draft, and Rising Stars participants doubling into other events may play reduced minutes.
nba.rising_stars_roster_strength.measurement: Per player: offensive impact per 100 possessions this season (box-score composite) shrunk to a draft-slot prior with weight k = number of possessions at which sampling variance equals prior variance (estimate from rookie seasons 2015-2025, not 800 by assumption). G League players: rating x translation factor estimated as the regression slope of NBA first-year impact on prior G League impact over players who moved between leagues (report the estimate and its se; use 1.0 shrunk toward 0.7 if fewer than 30 players). Team strength = sum over rostered players of minute share x rating with minutes from nba.asg_minutes_rotation_plan; output per-possession scoring rate and sd for nba.target_score_race_model. As-of: Rising Stars draft and final roster announcement.
free_sources: Basketball-Reference rookie and G League stats
nba.rising_stars_roster_strength.why: The Rising Stars series (and the 2025 ASG's fourth team) settles on these teams, which no NBA team rating covers.

nba.shooting_stars_team_skill.label: Shooting Stars team shooting skill and format conversion
nba.shooting_stars_team_skill.mechanism: A Shooting Stars team (franchise-named; recent editions mixed current players with retired or other-league shooters) scores by making shots from a sequence of locations within a time limit; the team with the higher score wins.
nba.shooting_stars_team_skill.rationale: Kalshi's rules give only team and date; the league's official 2026 Shooting Stars rules PDF (read and hashed 2026-11-09) gives the full format: four teams of three (two NBA players plus one NBA Legend), seven locations in fixed order worth 2/2/2/3/2/3/4 points, 1:10 clock, top two of four advance, 30-second first-round tiebreaker, full 1:10 final tiebreaker, disqualification and out-of-order rules. What stays unknown is how Kalshi applies those rules to settlement and, from the PDF itself, what counts as a valid shot attempt, what disqualification does to a team's score or advancement, and whether the 30-second tiebreaker still runs locations 1-6 in full. A Legend is likely to have little or no current shooting data, so team skill mixes current catch-and-shoot rates for active players with older evidence; tempo matters as in the 3PT contest.
nba.shooting_stars_team_skill.measurement: 2026 format (official NBA rules PDF, ak-static.cms.nba.com 2026-Kia-Shooting-Stars-Rules.pdf, sha256 ed035e65...b921): four teams of three, two NBA players plus one NBA Legend (the PDF does not say the players must be current); seven locations shot in order 1 to 7 (right-lane layup/dunk 2, 18-ft right baseline 2, right elbow 2, right-wing three 3, top of the key 2, left-corner three 3, long-range three 4); each player takes one shot at each of locations 1-6 in the team's declared order, then at location 7 players shoot in that order as many times as the clock allows; a passer feeds each shot; the team advances as a unit; 1:10 clock; round 1 all four teams, top two to the final; the lower round-1 team shoots first in the final and the higher final-round score wins (the PDF says the round-1 score is ignored only in the tiebreaker; that the final score alone decides is an inference from the wording). Current players: P(make) by spot from nba.threept_spot_and_tempo_profile. Legend component: last five career seasons' 3P% and FT% with an age discount of 1.5 points of 3P% per year since retirement, shrunk to the past legends' contest make rate with k = 50 shots; a shot-tempo term for the legend's attempts within the clock. Score = 2*(makes at locations 1, 2, 3, 5) + 3*(makes at locations 4, 6) + 4*(makes at location 7); a shot out of declared order scores zero and (locations 1-6) its shooter does not shoot again, and a team that does not have all three players make valid attempts at a location, or that shoots from locations out of order, is disqualified (the PDF gives no definition of a valid attempt and no consequence for the team's score or advancement beyond the word disqualified). Round-1 ties that decide advancement go to a 30-second rerun among only the tied teams (round-1 scores ignored); a tied final is rerun for the full 1:10. Simulate 20,000 contests under this rule set and report P(win) with a disqualification and out-of-order branch whose size is an assumption (EMPIRICAL_QUESTION; the consequence of disqualification is not stated); the number of location-7 attempts per player inside 70 seconds and the legend's rate remain estimates (EMPIRICAL_QUESTION), and the Kalshi-specific treatment of disqualification, replay and cancellation stays unknown.
free_sources: NBA.com Shooting Stars announcements and recaps
raw_data: current-season shot-location data for active players
nba.shooting_stars_team_skill.why: KXNBASHOOTINGSTARS settles on this contest and no other input models a team shooting relay.

sources.name: NBA 2026 Kia Shooting Stars official rules (PDF): format, 7 locations and 2/3/4 point values, 1:10 clock, tiebreakers, violations
sources.note: primary source for the 2026 event; verbatim extract and rendered-table reading in completeness/source_provenance/; says nothing about how Kalshi settles ties, disqualification, replay or cancellation

nba.asg_mvp_vote_model.label: All-Star MVP selection model (production on the winning team and voter choice)
nba.asg_mvp_vote_model.mechanism: The All-Star MVP is chosen by a selection panel after the event; winners almost always come from the champion team and are the standout scorer or narrative figure, so P(MVP) = P(team wins) x P(selected | team wins, box score, narrative).
nba.asg_mvp_vote_model.rationale: In a tournament with short games the MVP depends on the whole path, and home-market or farewell narratives can beat raw points. The selection method (media panel, any fan component) and whether it covers only the championship game are not in the Kalshi rules, and a withdrawn named player resolves No.
nba.asg_mvp_vote_model.measurement: 2026 rule: media panel vote right after the championship game combined with a 25% in-game fan vote; scope = the whole tournament (Edwards 2026, totals across three games, 10 of 14 panel votes). Panel part: P(panel pick) = sum over teams P(team wins the tournament) from nba.asg_tournament_path_sim x conditional logit over that team's players on tournament points share, made threes, minutes, home-market flag and prior All-Star MVP (fit on 20+ events), plus a residual for a non-champion MVP from the historical share; final score = 0.75 x panel share + 0.25 x nba.asg_mvp_fan_vote_share; multiply by P(participates). As-of: final rosters.
free_sources: Basketball-Reference All-Star MVP history and box scores
raw_data: Starter status, home-market flag, prior MVP flag
nba.asg_mvp_vote_model.why: KXNBAALLSTARMVP settles on this award, which depends on both the tournament winner and the panel's choice.

nba.asg_mvp_fan_vote_share.label: All-Star MVP in-game fan vote share (25% of the MVP decision)
nba.asg_mvp_fan_vote_share.mechanism: The All-Star MVP is decided by a media panel voting right after the championship game plus a fan vote that counts 25%, so a popular player on the winning team can win with a weaker box score than the panel favourite.
nba.asg_mvp_fan_vote_share.rationale: 2026 coverage: fans counted 25% and the panel gave Edwards 10 of 14 votes, with the award covering the whole three-game tournament. The fan vote is cast during the event, not in the January starter ballot, so it depends on popularity plus visible tournament moments; the January fan-ballot rank is only a prior for it.
nba.asg_mvp_fan_vote_share.measurement: Per participant on each team: fan_share = softmax over the team's players of (a x log January All-Star fan-ballot votes from the last published returns + b x tournament points share + c x home-market flag), a, b, c fitted on past All-Star MVP fan-vote outcomes where published (else fixed a=1, b=2, c=0.3 as placeholders labelled unverified); MVP score = 0.75 x panel vote share (from nba.asg_mvp_vote_model) + 0.25 x fan_share; P(MVP) from 10,000 tournament draws. As-of: final rosters; fan-ballot snapshot dated.
raw_data: All-Star fan-ballot vote totals by player (January returns)
All-Star MVP results and reported vote splits
nba.asg_mvp_fan_vote_share.why: Carries the 25% in-game fan vote that decides KXNBAALLSTARMVP alongside the media panel.

nba.all_star_process.reason: Captain, roster and event participation set who is eligible to win each series; it does not give shooting or judging ability, so it is a gate not a driver.

nba.allstar_reserve_coach_vote.reason: Only matters to the Game market through who is on rosters, and the vote is mostly settled before pricing; use as roster provenance, not as a performance input.

nba.player_impact.reason: Regular-season impact overstates defenders in a no-defence Game; keep only offensive components and only for the All-Star Game series; irrelevant to contests and Rising Stars (separate input).

nba.injuries_pit.reason: Withdrawals, replacements and reduced minutes are the main pregame information events for all three series; official report vintages are required.

nba.news.reason: Fields, formats and captain choices appear in reporting before official announcements; keep with reporter-reliability weighting rather than as a performance signal.

nba.three_volume.reason: For the 3PT contest it duplicates the openness prior and location profile (volume is usage, not accuracy), so it is scoped to the All-Star Game roster offence only, as context.

nba.three_make_by_openness_prior.reason: Open and wide-open make rate is the nearest game proxy for contest rack shooting; it has to be rescaled via the contest transfer input.

nba.within_game_make_dispersion.reason: Supplies the within-round make correlation that widens contest score variance; estimated from games so only a prior for a one-minute stationary round.

nba.ft_skill_posterior.reason: Free-throw skill correlates with stationary shooting form but is weak across shot distance; a context feature for the contest and unused for dunks and the Game.

nba.venue.reason: Home-court effects do not apply to neutral All-Star sites, but backdrop and rim feel matter for contest conversion; use as venue-year offset only.

nba.rule_change_pipeline.reason: Provides early notice of format changes announced by the league; only context because the format ledger is the decisive record once the format is announced.

nba.calendar_announcements.reason: Sets the as-of discipline: rosters, fields and formats are announced on known dates and features must not use later information.

m.rules_text.reason: Rules text is now sampled for all seven series; it fixes withdrawal-to-No, the 70 s round, dunk round structure, 12-minute round robin and 40/25 targets, and exposes empty text for two series.

m.settlement_truth.reason: The official winner announcement is the label; useful for reconciling ties, shoot-offs and disputes about which entrant counts.

nba.voting_narrative.reason: Only for the MVP series: home-market and farewell narratives shift the panel's choice among winning-team players beyond points; irrelevant to contests and team winners.

nba.usage.reason: Only for the MVP series: shot share inside the exhibition decides who posts the standout line on the champion team; irrelevant to rack shooting and judged dunks.

interactions.mechanism: Win probability is a max-of-noisy-scores function of per-ball make rates, so a shooter's gain from a few points of make probability is bigger when the field is thin at the top and shrinks as more strong shooters enter.
interactions.how_to_test: Simulate the field with and without the best entrant and compare the change in each remaining entrant's P(win); check against historical favourite hit rates by field strength spread.

interactions.mechanism: Judged score saturates near the scale maximum, so extra difficulty adds little once a clean dunk already earns near-perfect marks, while a miss subtracts a lot; this reverses the naive hard-dunk advantage.
interactions.how_to_test: Regress dunk score on difficulty tier and make flag with a ceiling-aware ordinal model and compare the marginal effect of tier among clean dunks versus the miss penalty.

interactions.mechanism: Win probability is the roster gap divided by margin SD, and the SD depends on format length and late effort, so the same gap gives a smaller edge in a shorter or more effort-compressed format.
interactions.how_to_test: Compute z = gap / SD for each past exhibition and test the win rate by z bucket and format length.

interactions.mechanism: A withdrawal changes the winner probability differently depending on the number of finalists and rounds: with fewer rounds a replacement has a larger chance to win through variance.
interactions.how_to_test: Compare historical outcomes for replacement entrants against the pre-event field ranking, split by number of rounds.

interactions.mechanism: A star with a minor injury often plays a sharply reduced role or none, so impact on team strength is a threshold at the status level, not a gradual one.
interactions.how_to_test: Estimate minutes by injury status tier in past exhibitions and test the roster composite with a status-tier discount versus a linear one.

interactions.mechanism: In the 2026 round robin a team only needs margin when all three finish 1-1, so the value of a roster edge switches from win probability to expected point differential in that branch; a deep team that runs up the score on the weakest opponent gains disproportionately.
interactions.how_to_test: In the simulation compare champion probability under win-only versus margin-aware ranking, and check past round-robin exhibitions for margin-chasing in decided games.

interactions.mechanism: A per-possession scoring edge converts concavely into win probability in a race to 25 because there are few possessions; the same Rising Stars roster edge yields a larger edge in the 40-point semifinal than in the 25-point final.
interactions.how_to_test: Simulate fixed per-possession edges at targets 25 and 40 and compare with realised win rates of favoured sides in past target-score exhibitions.

interactions.mechanism: MVP probability is the product of the player's team reaching and winning the championship and his conditional selection share, so a dominant individual scorer on an underdog team stays priced low while a moderate scorer on a heavy favourite rises.
interactions.how_to_test: Back-test past All-Star MVPs: fraction from the winning team and the conditional-logit fit of selection share given team win.

interactions.mechanism: The gain from placing the all-money rack at a shooter's best location depends on the ball values and whether deep bonus balls exist in that year's format; a large location split is worth more when money balls carry double value and less when deep balls dominate the maximum.
interactions.how_to_test: Simulate expected round score with optimal versus average rack placement under each historical format vector and compare with announced placements and realised scores.

interactions.mechanism: Team score is a weighted sum of correct-order makes at seven locations worth 2/2/2/3/2/3/4 points; a shot taken out of the declared player order does not count, and a team is disqualified if not all players make valid attempts at a location or if it shoots from locations out of order. The PDF states these rules but not what disqualification does to the score or to advancement, and does not define a valid attempt, so a disqualification branch is a modelling assumption whose size must be estimated, and the location-7 attempt count (unlimited ordered attempts until the clock expires) is a free-running count whose contribution to variance is an empirical question.
interactions.how_to_test: Simulate the 2026 rules with and without the disqualification and out-of-order branch and with location-7 attempts fixed versus clock-limited; compare the change in each team's P(top two) and P(win) and check which branch moves rankings most. Calibrate the branch frequencies against the recorded 2026 round scores (empirical, not assumed here).

interactions.mechanism: Locations 1-6 give each player exactly one attempt while location 7 (4 points) allows ordered attempts until the clock expires, so the rules let a faster early sequence leave more clock for location 7; a team's expected score is then the one-shot sum plus the completed location-7 attempts times the 4-point make rate. Whether the clock ever binds before location 7 and how large the location-7 share of variance is are not stated by the rules and are empirical questions (threshold-like gain assumed, not verified).
interactions.how_to_test: Using the recorded 2026 round videos or scores, regress team score on location-7 attempt count and on elapsed time at the start of location 7; compare with a simulation that varies the time spent on locations 1-6. Paused phase: this is a test design, not a result.

interactions.mechanism: The format has tie-resolution regimes: a round-1 tie that decides advancement is rerun with a 30-second clock among tied teams only (round-1 scores ignored), while a final tie is rerun for the full 1:10, so the tiebreaker rewards different skills (fewer shots in 30 seconds shifts weight from location 7 to the one-shot locations).
interactions.how_to_test: Simulate P(win) for tied pairs under a 30-second clock versus a 1:10 clock and measure how the ranking of the Legend-weighted versus NBA-player-weighted teams changes; confirm the rules wording in the league PDF for each tie case.

nonlinearities.shape: Convex in P(win) near the top of the field, flat for low skill
nonlinearities.why: The winner is the maximum of several noisy scores, so top shooters gain disproportionally from higher make rates while low-skill entrants have almost no chance regardless of small skill changes.

nonlinearities.shape: Ceiling at the maximum score with heavy tie mass
nonlinearities.why: Scores are bounded and compressed at the top, so differences in dunk quality translate into almost no score difference above a threshold and the winner is then decided by ties and dunk-offs.

nonlinearities.shape: Regime-dependent: late variance compression in timed games only
nonlinearities.why: In timed 12-minute games defensive effort rises near the end, lowering final-minute margin variance; in target-score races there is no clock and the end is a first-passage threshold, so the same compression term must be zero there.

nonlinearities.shape: Threshold at the target with overshoot
nonlinearities.why: The game ends the moment a team reaches 25 or 40, so the probability of winning jumps discretely with a made three near the target and possession order matters more than average efficiency.
Because withdrawal resolves No, a named entrant's Yes probability is capped by P(participates), which falls sharply with an injury status change rather than linearly.

nonlinearities.shape: Piecewise: possible disqualification and out-of-order branches (consequence unstated), plus a count-driven location-7 tail
nonlinearities.why: Score is a fixed one-shot sum from locations 1-6 plus a clock-limited count of 4-point attempts at location 7, and an out-of-order shot removes its points while a disqualification (consequence not stated in the PDF) could cut the score discontinuously, so small differences in make rate or tempo need not map linearly to P(win).

unresolved.description: Format details not in rules text are from memory: 3PT ball values (money balls, deep-zone balls) and rack count, dunk judging scale and dunk-off rule, 2025 ASG four-team target-score format, and the 2026 round-robin tiebreak after point differential.
unresolved.what_would_resolve: Read the league's official format releases for each event-year and record each field in the format ledger with provenance.

unresolved.description: Ball-by-ball contest data and per-dunk judge scores are not provided in a structured public table, so the round-score correlation and judge model would rely on hand coding of video.
unresolved.what_would_resolve: Locate a structured source or hand-code recent contests to sizes sufficient to estimate rho and judge effects.

unresolved.description: The effect of effort, prize incentives and fatigue on exhibition play is not measurable with any pregame variable defined here and the sample of games under the current format is very small.
unresolved.what_would_resolve: Collect more seasons under the current format and test candidate effort proxies such as late-game defence rate.

unresolved.description: KXNBAALLSTAR (2025) and KXNBASHOOTINGSTARS have only a one-line rules_primary: format, ties, non-participation of a named team and source of truth are unstated; KXNBAALLSTARGAME is silent on the tiebreak after point differential and on ties in 12-minute games.
unresolved.what_would_resolve: Sample current-year rules for these series or obtain Kalshi's clarification of the tie and team-change branches.

unresolved.description: The Celebrity Game was removed from contract_types because no live Kalshi series exists in the evidence pack; if one is listed it needs roster-composition and special-scoring inputs.
unresolved.what_would_resolve: Check the Kalshi series list each All-Star cycle and add an archetype or stage if a Celebrity Game series appears.

unresolved.description: Per-judge dunk scores (needed for the judge effect) may exist only on broadcast video, and combine verticals are missing for undrafted or G League dunk entrants; structured availability is unverified.
unresolved.what_would_resolve: Check NBA.com recaps, NBA Stats event pages and video for per-judge cards for 2015-2026 and count entrants lacking combine data.

unresolved.description: Contest entrants who also play Rising Stars or the All-Star Game (fatigue, reduced effort), home-market entrants and crowd influence on dunk judges are unmodelled for the skills contests.
unresolved.what_would_resolve: Tag past entrants by doubling-up and home-market status and test score residuals in the contest models.

unresolved.description: No existing blueprint fits the seven disjoint processes (game_side is chosen as nearest for the team tournaments); inputs are scoped per series in catalog_entry and contract.series_input_scope instead of splitting the archetype.
unresolved.what_would_resolve: Decide whether to split into contests, team exhibitions and MVP archetypes or add an exhibition blueprint.

unresolved.description: All-Star MVP selection method (media panel size, any fan-vote component) and whether it covers the championship game or the whole tournament are not in the rules and are unverified for the 2026 format.
unresolved.what_would_resolve: Read the NBA's MVP announcement and voting description for 2025 and 2026 and store it in the format ledger.

unresolved.description: Shooting Stars format (team size, locations and point values, time limit, rounds, ties) was absent from Kalshi's rules text, so nba.shooting_stars_team_skill could not simulate scores. Closed 2026-11-09 from the league's official 2026 rules PDF (sha256 ed035e65...b921; completeness/source_provenance/NBA_2026_Shooting_Stars.json): four trios, seven locations worth 2/2/2/3/2/3/4, 1:10 clock, top two advance, 30-second first-round tiebreaker, full 1:10 final tiebreaker, shot order and disqualification rules.
unresolved.what_would_resolve: Done: league rules PDF read and recorded. Kalshi-specific treatment is tracked separately as u10b.

unresolved.description: Kalshi's KXNBASHOOTINGSTARS text gives only the team name and the originally scheduled date, with an empty rules_secondary; its contract-terms link points at the Rising Stars file and could not be read here. The league PDF does not say how disqualification, ties beyond the two named tiebreakers, replay, a changed format or cancellation affect settlement, nor what a 'valid shot attempt' is, so Kalshi-specific application is unknown.
unresolved.what_would_resolve: Kalshi publishing or confirming settlement terms for the Shooting Stars series, or the league clarifying the validity and disqualification rules.
